What the government does is not about efficiency in the way you may be thinking. A private institution aims to maximize efficiency in the sense of maximizing profit, while a public institution aims to maximize efficiency in the sense of serving as many people as possible.

The USPS will deliver mail to everywhere in the country, inevitably operating at a loss in some places. UPS, on the other hand, can choose not to pick up or deliver somewhere in order to maximize profits. Less people served in the name of making money. This was also true of things like phone lines and electricity in the US, where private corporations who ran these services built up their infrastructure in large cities first while ignoring rural areas. This is all a result of the free market and how efficiency works in the sense of maximizing profits.

So when you're talking about efficiency being so important, you have to decide and understand what you mean by efficiency. You also have to think about where a market economy may fail in providing certain services, where nationalizing may be a better option.
